topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: In LEO, larger antenna apertures are beneficial due to lower free space path loss (FSPL) and smaller signal propagation time delay. However, this increases mutual coupling and interference between adjacent satellite beams, degrading system capacity and performance. Conversely, in GEO, fixed positions and wider earth surface coverage require smaller antenna apertures to mitigate interference effects and maintain link margin. The array factor of the antenna pattern is influenced by the number of elements, spacing, and phase shifts. Adaptive Beamforming (ABF) technology can dynamically adjust antenna patterns to compensate for signal propagation time delay and FSPL variations in both LEO and GEO satellite regimes.
